Architecture: where CPQ sits on the Salesforce platform

html:
CPQ — Configure, Price, Quote — is the engine that turns a sales conversation into a legally priced, contract-ready quote. Salesforce sells two engines under the umbrella "CPQ & Revenue Cloud": the mature managed-package CPQ (the classic SBQQ__ product) and the next-generation Revenue Lifecycle Management (RLM) platform built on core Salesforce objects. This first module of the CPQ & Revenue Cloud Academy maps the whole quote-to-cash lifecycle, shows where each engine fits, and gives you the working vocabulary and deployment path you will need for every later phase.

Everything you practice in this Academy lives in a source-controlled Salesforce DX project whose Apex services — QuoteCalculatorService, QuoteTriggerHandlerService, PriceRuleEngineService, BundleConfigurationService, and friends — mirror the real division of labor you will find in a production CPQ org. By the end of this guide you will have run your first quote through the full pipeline and understood which engine to reach for when.

Learning objectives

  • Describe the quote-to-cash lifecycle and where each object (Opportunity → Quote → QuoteLineItem → Contract → Order → Revenue Schedule) participates.
  • Distinguish the two quoting engines — managed-package CPQ and Revenue Cloud / RLM — and pick the right one for a scenario.
  • Explain the role of list price, net price, and the Discount_Percent__c calculation.
  • List the standard and custom objects that drive a CPQ quote in this project.
  • Map the Apex services to the lifecycle stage each one automates.
  • State the CPQ Specialist and Revenue Cloud Consultant exam facts (count, time, pass bar, price, blueprint).
  • Run the "golden path" test that pushes a quote through recalculation, approval events, billing, and recognition.
  • Identify the personas and process stages that CPQ serves.
  • Apply the pin factory of the Academy roadmap to your own study plan.

What CPQ means (Configure, Price, Quote)

CPQ is three problems solved in one workflow.

Configure — a product is rarely a single SKU. A laptop comes with a CPU choice, a memory choice, a storage option, and a service contract. The configurator constrains which combinations are legal (you can't have two hard disks in one slot) and which are required (every server must have an operating system). In this project, configuration constraints are exercised with product families, bundle parents, and option lines.

Price — once a valid configuration exists, the engine produces a price. The list price comes from the price book; discounts, volume tiers, contracts, and renewal uplifts modify it. The difference between list and net is the discount — and discount leakage is the single most-reported KPI in a CPQ rollout.

Quote — the priced configuration is packaged as a formal document: a quote with a header (customer, term, currency, approval state) and lines (product, quantity, list price, net price). The quote is the contract of record between sales and the rest of the revenue organization.

The two engines implement these three verbs differently:

CapabilityClassic CPQ (managed package)Revenue Cloud / RLM
ObjectsSBQQ__Quote__c, SBQQ__QuoteLine__c, SBQQ__ProductConfiguration__cCore Quote, QuoteLineItem, plus ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel
Configuration engineProduct rules, option constraints, bundle groupsCatalog + selling model with dynamic options
PricingPrice rules, discount schedules, block pricingPrice books + pricing logic on the selling model
Where it runsNamespaced managed package installed on top of platformNative platform features under "Revenue Cloud"
Best fitMature enterprise quote-to-cash, deep discounts, complex approvalsNet-new subscription selling on Sales Cloud data model
DeploymentPackage install + admin configurationFeature enablement + metadata
Tip — In certification exams there is no "better" engine, only "which is in use." Learn facts about both; the Revenue Cloud Consultant blueprint tests the core-data-model objects, while the CPQ Specialist blueprint tests the managed-package vocabulary (SBQQ__).

The quote-to-cash lifecycle

The lifecycle that CPQ lives inside is wider than quoting. This project's golden path test (CPQFundamentalsTest) walks a quote through every stage, so memorize the handoffs:

StagePrimary objectWhat happens
1. OpportunityOpportunityDeal is qualified; ARR__c and Current_ARR__c give revenue context
2. QuoteQuoteHeader: term, approval state, Total_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c
3. Line pricingQuoteLineItemQuantity × price; list vs net per line
4. ConfigureIs_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__cBundle parents roll up option prices
5. ApprovalApproval_Log__cApproval routing publishes a Revenue_Sync__e event on state change
6. ContractContractQuote generates a draft contract; renewal opportunities are created on expiry
7. BillingRevenue_Schedule__cStraight-line schedule rows spread the value over Contract_Term_Months__c
8. RecognitionRevenue_Schedule__cRecognition rolls recognized ARR up to Account.Current_ARR__c
9. OrderOrderFulfillment_Status__c moves Pending → Shipped → Delivered

Each arrow is a handoff where "output leaves sales and enters the back office." A quote is not finished when it is signed; it is finished when its revenue is recognized and its order is fulfilled.

Two engines: managed-package CPQ vs Revenue Cloud

The 2020s saw Salesforce progressively fold CPQ into a broader "Revenue Cloud" story. It matters to you because the certified-skill market splits along this line.

  • Classic CPQ is a managed package with namespaced objects (SBQQ__Quote__c, SBQQ__QuoteLine__c). Configuration happens through product rules and options; pricing through price rules and discount schedules; documents through quote templates. It is deep, battle-tested, and still the bulk of enterprise installs.
  • Revenue Cloud / RLM is native. Quoting uses the standard Quote and QuoteLineItem; the catalog is modeled with ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel, and PriceBookEntry. It is the platform direction for subscription-heavy businesses.

This Academy project deliberately builds on standard + custom objects (no SBQQ__ fields) so you can practice in a plain Developer org and still learn every concept. When a concept differs between engines, the guide calls it out — for example, bundle options are SBQQ__Optional__c lines in classic CPQ but are modeled here with a custom Bundle_Option__c text field on QuoteLineItem.

Decision you must makeClassic CPQ (SBQQ)Revenue Cloud / RLM
Install footprintManaged package + licenseFeature enablement, no namespace
Config modelSBQQ__Option__c hierarchyProductSellingModel dynamic options
Document generationQuote templates in packageNative quote templates
Exam you take for itCPQ Specialist / CPQ AdministratorRevenue Cloud Consultant

Architecture: where CPQ sits on the Salesforce platform

A CPQ implementation is platform features layered in a predictable stack:

  • Data layer — standard objects (Product, Pricebook, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Contract, Order) plus custom objects for your discount and revenue logic.
  • Logic layer — triggers stay thin and delegate to Apex services (the trigger-handler pattern), so business rules are unit-testable without firing triggers.
  • Workflow layer — approvals, flows, and platform events coordinate handoffs.
  • Presentation layer — Lightning apps, quote templates, and the configurator UI.

This repo implements the logic layer explicitly. For example, QuoteTriggerHandlerService is the single funnel for all Quote triggers; it defaults Contract_Term_Months__c to 12 on insert, normalizes nulls on update, and publishes a Revenue_Sync__e platform event whenever Approval_Status__c changes. Triggers never contain business logic.

apex
// QuoteTriggerHandlerService.beforeInsert — defaults, never business logic
public static void beforeInsert(List<Quote> newQuotes) {
    for (Quote q : newQuotes) {
        if (q.Approval_Status__c == null) {
            q.Approval_Status__c = 'Not Submitted';
        }
        if (q.Contract_Term_Months__c == null) {
            q.Contract_Term_Months__c = 12;
        }
    }
}
Tip — Follow the same pattern in your own projects: public with sharing classes, static @TestVisible hooks instead of global test seams, and recursion guards (shouldRun / clear) for any class a trigger re-enters.

Key personas and process stages

CPQ serves a chain of roles, and each role has different buttons:

PersonaWhat they touchTheir success metric
Sales repConfiguration UI, quote, discountFast, accurate quotes
Sales manager / VPApproval flows, discount leakageApproved margin, less leakage
Revenue / Billing opsContracts, orders, schedulesClean contract-to-cash handoff
Finance controllerRevenue recognition, ARR rollupsASC 606 / IFRS 15 compliance
Implementation consultantThe 8-point implementation loop (data, config, pricing, docs, approvals, contracts, orders, billing)On-time go-live

Implementation follows a repeatable sequence: map the process → design the data model → configure the catalog → price → template the documents → approve → contract → bill → recognize → hand to fulfillment. Every phase in the 17-module roadmap corresponds to one ring of this loop.

Discount leakage(sum(list) − sum(net)) / sum(list), the % of gross margin negotiated away

Hands-on walkthrough

This walkthrough uses the shipped Apex services and the data model — no managed package required. Everything you touch lives in force-app.

  1. Deploy the project. From the repo root, authorize a scratch or Developer org and push the metadata:

    text
    sf org create scratch --definition-file config/project-scratch-def.json --set-alias cpq-academy --duration-days 7
sf project deploy start --target-org cpq-academy
  2. Run the golden path test. Execute the full pipeline test from the CLI and confirm it is green:

    text
    sf apex run test --class-name CPQFundamentalsTest --test-level RunSpecifiedTests --target-org cpq-academy

    The suite asserts 4 seats × 800 net = Total_ARR__c 3200 with a 20% discount off a 4000 list total, an approval event, a draft contract, a 12-row billing schedule, an ARR rollup, and a Pending → Shipped → Delivered order.

  3. Watch the discount engine. In Anonymous Apex, insert a portion of the test data yourself and call QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals:

    apex
    Quote q = [SELECT Id, Total_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c FROM Quote LIMIT 1];
QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(new Set<Id>{ q.Id });
System.debug(q.Total_ARR__c + ' | ' + q.Discount_Percent__c);
  4. Trigger the event publish. Flip the approval state and confirm Revenue_Sync__e fired (the handler publishes one event per changed quote):

    apex
    Quote q = [SELECT Id, Approval_Status__c FROM Quote LIMIT 1];
q.Approval_Status__c = 'Approved';
update q;

    The afterUpdate handler builds a Revenue_Sync__e with Source_Object__c = 'Quote', Direction__c = 'Outbound', Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync', and a JSON payload containing quote id, approval status, total ARR, and discount percent.

  5. Prove the recursion guard. Re-run step 4 twice in one transaction; the second publish is skipped because shouldRun('QuoteApprovalSync') returns false on re-entry — a bug you would otherwise chase as an infinite trigger loop.

  6. Query your evidence:

    soql
    SELECT Id, Source_Object__c, Direction__c, Integration_Type__c, Status__c, Payload__c
FROM Revenue_Sync__e
ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC

Common pitfalls

  • Treating the two engines as interchangeable. Classic CPQ (SBQQ__) and RLM use different objects, config models, and exams. On a client project, ask which engine is installed before quoting object names.
  • Logic inside triggers. A trigger that recalculates totals inline is untestable and recursive. Always funnel through a handler service with a recursion guard.
  • Ignoring list vs net. Discount leakage hides when nobody tracks the list baseline. Keep both List_Unit_Price__c and Net_Unit_Price__c on every line.
  • Publishing events in a loop. EventBus.publish outside a single gathered batch multiplies event API calls and jumbles correlation. Gather, then publish once.
  • Skipping boundary guards. Real services accept null and empty batches without throwing (recalculateTotals(null) is safe). Prove it in a test like fundamentals_edge_emptyInputsNeverThrow.
  • Studying the wrong blueprint. 105 minutes and 60 questions are shared by both exams, but the pass marks differ (65% vs 62%) and the domains are completely different.

Key takeaways

  • CPQ = Configure, Price, Quote; the quote-to-cash lifecycle continues past the quote through contract, billing, recognition, and fulfillment.
  • There are two engines — managed-package CPQ (SBQQ__) and Revenue Cloud / RLM (core objects) — and you must be able to reason about both.
  • In this Academy the data model is standard + custom objects, so every exercise runs on a plain Developer org.
  • QuoteCalculatorService owns totals and discount math; QuoteTriggerHandlerService owns trigger entry points and event publishing; triggers stay thin.
  • Discount leakage is (list − net) / list and is the KPI the entire pricing engine defends.
  • The two certifications (CPQ Specialist 65% / Revenue Cloud Consultant 62%, each 60 scored + up to 5 unscored in 105 minutes at USD 200) split by engine — use their blueprints as your curriculum.
  • Next: product catalog and configuration, where the configurator decides which products and options are quotable in the first place.
